what: [LOUD] TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS ON THE REAL-MONEY TRADE SURFACE, both of which have ALREADY produced a wrong operator-facing conclusion (2026-09-08, MI-200). Read this BEFORE measuring real-money performance. (1) THE POPULATION. GET /api/bot/trades/closed takes include_paper, DEFAULT False, so the default response is ALREADY real-money-only. Passing include_paper=true and then filtering to accountClass=='real_money' does NOT widen the real-money set — it NARROWS it to whatever fraction of the newest `limit` MIXED rows happens to be real money. Measured: ?limit=200 -> 200 real-money rows; ?limit=200&include_paper=true -> 15 real-money rows; paged to exhaustion -> 447, window 2026-05-09..2026-09-04. A dispatch reported the 15 as 'the real-money population' and concluded '0 wins, 13 losses'. The book is actually 117 W / 258 L / 49 flat (n=424 graded). The failure is SILENT: 200 OK, every row genuinely real money, nothing says the set was truncated. (2) THE LABEL. `closeReason` on that route folds FIFTEEN distinct mechanisms into `other`, including 182 rows that ARE strategy exits (vwap_cross, sl_cross, tp_cross, exit_head, time_decay, stale_stop). Reading `other` as 'not a strategy exit' is wrong in BOTH directions. /api/bot/strategies uses a DIFFERENT taxonomy over the SAME column and the two disagree on 174 of 447 rows (38.9%); 53 rows read `sl` on one surface and `other` on the other. Read RAW trades.exit_reason, never closeReason, to answer 'did the strategy's exit fire?'.
